new_statements.quote: [p. 18] C'est ainsi que des unités plus vastes que la syllabe comme le mot phonologique et la phrase phonologique n'ont pas été abordés; pas plus que la distribution des phonèmes dans la syllabe et dans le mot phonologique. [p. 19] Comme la question des tonèmes est toujours sous étude (1) le ton en général n'a pas été écrit, sauf là où cela était nécessaire pour montrer des oppositions. Là où il est écrit sa notation est souvent préliminaire (notation au moyen de chiffres: 1 = haut, 2 = mi-haut, 3 = mi-bas, 4 = bas). [...] 2. LA SYLLABE. La syllabe en ditammari est définie comme une unité de durée. Son noyau, qui porte un ton, peut étre une voyelle ou une consonne nasale syllabique.
new_statements.translation: [p. 18] Thus units larger than the syllable, such as the phonological word and the phonological phrase, have not been dealt with; nor has the distribution of phonemes within the syllable and within the phonological word. [p. 19] Since the question of the tonemes is still under study (1), tone has in general not been written, except where it was necessary to show oppositions. Where it is written its notation is often preliminary (notation by means of digits: 1 = high, 2 = mid-high, 3 = mid-low, 4 = low). [...] 2. THE SYLLABLE. The syllable in Ditammari is defined as a unit of duration. Its nucleus, which bears a tone, may be a vowel or a syllabic nasal consonant.

new_statements.relation_note: Catalog has no record for dita1238; the work adds nothing on stress, only that the language is tonal (four pitch levels, provisional) and that the phonological word was not studied. Note the listed open_url (SIL archive 19060) is a wrong item (Kondo 1978, Guahibo discourse); the correct SIL entry is 2725, found via the sil.org site search; the PDF itself is behind an automated-access block and was obtained from the Internet Archive copy of 2025-01-20.
new_statements.rule_in_words: The paper is a segmental phonology only: it treats Ditammari as a tone language (every syllable nucleus bears a tone; provisional four-level pitch notation, tonemes under study) and explicitly excludes the phonological word. No mention of stress, accent, prominence or intensity anywhere in the 41 pages (searched the scanned for accent, proéminence, intensité, hauteur, tonique, force). The only prosodic content is tone and syllable duration (long vowels analysed as two syllables).
new_statements.identity_note: Zürcher 1983 states in its first footnote (p. 18) that the article was written after a short stay at Nadoba (Préfecture de la Kéran, Togo) with two Nadoba speakers supplying the corpus, so it describes the Togo (Western, 'Tamberma') variety of Ditammari, although the SIL archive metadata for both entries says 'Country: Benin'. Zürcher & Nicole 1983 (same SIL Togo volume) presumably describes the same variety.

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Zürcher 1983 (the work marked silent) does say something about accent: pp. 39-43 (PDF pp. 26-30) condition allophones on accented vs non-accented syllables and mark accent with the IPA stress mark in transcriptions. p. 39: /k/ [k] 'après des voyelles phonétiquement courtes, non-nasalisées et accentuées' ([di-'kaka] 'la cuisine', [ku-'pi-ku] 'le flanc'); p. 40: [g] after 'une voyelle phonétiquement courte non-accentuée'; p. 41: [ɩ], [ɨ] 'dans des syllabes non-accentuées' ([dɩ'bɔ:] /di'bɔɔ/ 'le grenier', [si'mi:bi] /si'miibi/ 'la source', ['mɛtriba] 'les maîtres', [di'ŋwãni] 'le nez', /di'kwa/ 'marché'); p. 42: [ʊ], [ə] 'dans des syllabes non-accentuées' (/diŋwãtidi/ 'l'étoile' as [di'ŋwãtiři…
